first.rationale: Two of the three current symptoms are funnel-mechanical (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and the inherited record converges from two independent points (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on signup field reduction) that friction reduction lifts completion and first-week activation. That is the direction most likely to produce durable qualified revenue rather than borrowed revenue. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the single most load-bearing claim for the action I intend and is a consolidated summary whose original effect size, sample, and durability window I cannot see; if the archived record shows the lift was small, short-lived, or confounded with a concurrent change, my intended action should move. I am verifying memory_73 because promotional pricing is the obvious reflex to a competitor's entry pricing and is the strongest rival for the slot; its summary reports 'acquisition and revenue lift' but says nothing about retention or margin of discount-acquired accounts, which is exactly where the downstream value risk sits. Discount-led acquisition can raise near-term booked revenue while lowering revenue quality, and it also anchors price expectations in a way that is hard to unwind, so I am not spending the only slot of the week on it without seeing whether the original record tracked cohort retention. I am not verifying memory_57 or memory_44 because referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist do not address either declining metric, so their truth value would not change this week's decision. I run this as a standard experiment with a held-back control rather than a broad rollout: the inherited memories are summaries consolidated at days 12 and 52, product and segment mix have since shifted, and the current decline may itself indicate that the earlier onboarding gains have decayed or that a new friction source exists that field-cutting will not touch. I will treat the memory-based prior as a starting hypothesis to be re-measured on current traffic, not as settled fact, and I will instrument first-week activation and a 30-day retention/qualification proxy so the result distinguishes real time-to-value improvement from merely pushing weaker accounts further down the funnel.
